reading.rtitle: Supplier Security Questionnaire -- Vetra Distribuzione, Milan
paras: Section A -- Data storage. All customer data must be stored inside the European Union. Please state the country and the city where your servers are located. Data that is stored outside the EU cannot be accepted, and suppliers that store data outside the EU will be removed from the shortlist.
Section B -- Encryption. Customer data must be encrypted at rest and in transit. Please describe how your encryption keys are managed and which employees can access them.

Section C -- Access. Access to production systems should be limited to named employees. Two-factor authentication must be used for every account. When an employee leaves your company, all of their permissions must be removed within 24 hours.

Section D -- Backups and incidents. Backups should be tested at least once a quarter. Any security incident must be reported to Vetra within 48 hours. Please explain how a vulnerability is found, reported and fixed in your product.

Section E -- Audits and retention. Please attach your most recent certification, for example ISO 27001, and the date of your last external audit. Tell us how long invoice data is retained after the contract ends, and how it can be deleted at our request.
reading.source: Alumni by Better -- questionnaire written for this lesson, in the format European companies send to software suppliers

gist.prompt: What is this document mainly for?
choices: To explain Vetra's own IT systems and security rules to the new employees who join the company.
To check if a supplier protects data well enough to be accepted.
To negotiate the price of the software license.

items.situation: The form says: data must be stored in the EU. Tell Giulia where Invent's data is stored.
tips: Our data is stored in Frankfurt, so it is inside the EU.
Present passive for a fact: is stored.

items.situation: Make it a rule: all data / encrypt / must.
Say what is possible: permissions / remove / can / in one hour.
tips: Permissions can be removed in one hour.

items.situation: Make it a negative rule: data / store outside the EU / cannot.
tips: Data cannot be stored outside the EU.

items.situation: Giulia asks for the audit report, and it is not ready. Promise it for Friday.
tips: The audit report will be sent to you by Friday.
will + be + past participle for a promise.

items.situation: Ask the IT lead a question: how often / backups / should / test?
tips: How often should backups be tested?
Question: modal + subject + be + past participle.

listenings.text: I read about forty security questionnaires a year from suppliers, and I can tell in five minutes which ones I can trust. The bad answers are long and vague. They say things like we take security very seriously. That sentence tells me nothing. The good answers are short and specific. Where is the data stored? In Frankfurt. Is it encrypted? Yes, at rest and in transit. How fast can permissions be removed? On the same day. And when the supplier does not have something yet, the good answer is honest: the report will be sent next month. Do not leave a question empty, and do not copy the marketing text from your website. A questionnaire is not a sales document. It is a promise, and every promise you write there can be checked in an audit.

Two years ago I nearly lost my biggest deal because of a security questionnaire. The customer sent it on a Monday, and I passed it to our IT team without reading it. Three weeks later it was still not answered, and the customer's procurement team asked if we were still interested. Now I do it differently. I read the questionnaire on the day it arrives, and I mark three kinds of questions. Questions that can be answered by sales, like where our offices are. Questions that must be answered by IT, like how encryption keys are managed. And questions that should be discussed with the customer, because the requirement is not clear. Then I send a short email with a date: the full answers will be sent by Friday. The customer knows the deal is alive, and I know who owns every question.
